name: Symmetrical Cinematic Composition
visualIdentity: Normalized from a Grand Budapest Hotel reference; the source videos were not all assessed. Use axial symmetry, frontal framing, theatrical sets, carefully selected colors, and deliberately arranged props. Adapt the composition principles without copying a film scene or applying a generic pastel filter.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to staged scenes; suggested combinations include brand storytelling on miniature diorama sets and centered letterpress chapter cards. Inferred suitability includes video or interactive HTML when frontal staging and restrained movement support the subject.
limitations: Avoid oblique views when symmetry matters. Camera tilt may break isometric projection; movement must not expose incomplete layers, break ground contact, obscure labels, or make depth hard to read. Use chapter transitions only when narrative boundaries help; omit them if they obscure causality or violate a continuous-shot or loop requirement.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Resolve colors from task-provided exact colors, approved brand or reference palettes, existing semantic roles, then the optional example: background #EEE0C8, foreground #39494B, accent_1 #8B9A81, accent_2 #B97D66. Keep these discrete; gradients are disabled. Preserve approved colors, roles, families, and asset colors. The foreground on the example background has contrast 7.239; accents are decorative, not body-text backgrounds. Recheck actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use stable, symmetric camera placement, measured lateral moves, push-ins, and ordered character actions. Keep movement deliberate; preserve cuts, impacts, and reading holds where appropriate. Optional miniature parallax needs suitable depth layers and bounded offsets; optional chapter handoffs or story steps must share progress and resolve coherently in reverse. Pointer and scroll input are for interactive HTML; video uses deterministic, seekable composition time.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and user requirements. Synchronize audio and picture; keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Arrange props and characters deliberately; use theatrical set artwork or models. Diorama combinations need layered or pre-rendered miniature scenes; parallax requires supported depth layers, and a creature hop is optional only when suitable assets exist. Letterpress cards need centered type. Load fonts and assets and seed randomness for reproducible output.
combinations: Works alone for staged scenes. Suggested hybrid: style-079 miniature diorama sets, maintaining axial symmetry and avoiding oblique views; suitable for brand storytelling and frontal lateral moves. Style-052 letterpress chapter cards add tactile intertitles; keep type centered and avoid deep bevels.
productionApproach: Choose style rendering and motion methods by visual fidelity and scene needs: Blender with bpy and Cycles or EEVEE for 3D, or balanced 2D illustration; Blender is also a suggested motion engine. HyperFrames is the primary assembly, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic separate from the pipeline. For video, make state seekable and inspect representative frames and the full render; for interactive HTML, use live pointer or scroll behavior only where applicable. Suggested motion references are optional and must fit the actual scene.
